data.exact_reserve_text: In settling claims provisions the Syndicate gives consideration to the probability and magnitude of future experience being more adverse than assumed and exercises a degree of caution in setting reserves where there is considerable uncertainty. In general, the uncertainty associated with the ultimate claims experience in an underwriting year is greatest when the underwriting year is at an early stage of development and the margin necessary to provide the necessary confidence in the provisions adequacy is relatively at its highest. As claims develop, and the ultimate cost of claims becomes more certain, the relative level of margin maintained should decrease. However, due to the uncertainty inherent in the estimation process, the actual overall claim provision may not always be in surplus. In 2016 the surplus was GBP 14.6m.

data.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate opened 2016 with gross claims outstanding of GBP 95.413m (closing 2015 balance). During 2016 the Syndicate recorded significant current-year catastrophe losses (notably Hurricane Matthew, Alberta fires and a New Zealand earthquake) which materially affected the combined ratio. At the same time the Syndicate's prior years overall experience produced a reported surplus on provisions (the report states "In 2016 the surplus was GBP 14.6m"), reflecting favourable development on earlier years and releases as risk expired and large prior losses settled. The movement exhibits both large current-year catastrophe deterioration and favourable prior-year development, with the overall prior-year release described qualitatively but no single explicit gross prior-year movement figure provided in the notes.
raw_causal_phrases: 2016 saw a series of large losses which severely impacted the calendar year combined ratio, driving it up to 101.5% from 71.3%. These losses included Hurricane Matthew, fires in Alberta, and the New Zealand Earthquake.
The prudent reserving policy of the Syndicate in prior years enabled releases as risk expired or large losses were settled, which contributed to underwriting results on an annualised basis.

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from Balance Sheet (Claims outstanding 31 Dec 2015 = GBP 95,413k). The report does not present an explicit single-line gross prior-year movement figure in the 'Movement in prior year's provision' note; the available reserve movement disclosures include P&L 'Changes in claims outstanding' (gross change during year, includes current-year movement) and a net claims development triangle. The report states a prior-year surplus of GBP 14.6m (verbatim) but does not provide the gross insurance-liabilities column movement explicitly. The claims development table included in the notes is presented on a NET basis (cumulative net claims) in the document, so a reliable aggregated gross prior-year development number could not be unambiguously extracted; prior_year_development_gbp_m is therefore set to null.
